title: China drives Australia's coking coal export growth, but can demand hold?
section_path: China drives Australia's coking coal export growth, but can demand hold?
section_path_text: China drives Australia's coking coal export growth, but can demand hold?
summary:
Main
By Esther Chua
Australian Coking Coal shipments rose 8.6% in the year to 24 November, with China taking nearly nine-tenths of the increase despite weaker Chinese ironmaking. Imports can support loadings as mills replace domestic supply or rebuild stocks; repeat orders determine whether that support lasts. Through 22 December, Whitehaven's delayed Queensland sales could lift departures as producer stocks clear.

children.title: Steel output gives an uneven demand signal
section_path: Steel output gives an uneven demand signal
children.section_path_text: Steel output gives an uneven demand signal
children.summary:
Image reference: Στιγμιότυπο οθόνης 2026-11-27 102326.png | assets/2026-11-27_china-drives-australias-coking-coal-export-growth-but-can-demand-hold_img_cea3cf84ceb9ceb3cebcceb9cf8ccf84cf85_361ff7d9e259.png
China and Japan's January-October crude-steel output fell; India, South Korea and Vietnam grew (Figure 1). These totals include routes not requiring Coking Coal.

children.title: Growth depends on one market
children.summary: Australia shipped 144.6 Mt of Coking Coal between 1 January and 24 November 2026, against 133.2 Mt over the same dates in 2025. Shipments to China nearly doubled, from 10.5 Mt to 20.7 Mt.

children.title: Among the main buyers, only China has grown since September
section_path: Among the main buyers, only China has grown since September
children.section_path_text: Among the main buyers, only China has grown since September
children.summary: From 1 September to 24 November, total Australian shipments were almost unchanged on a year earlier, at 38.2 Mt against 37.8 Mt. Shipments to China rose 95.9% to 8.9 Mt.

children.title: China bought more while its ironmaking fell
section_path: China bought more while its ironmaking fell
children.section_path_text: China bought more while its ironmaking fell
children.summary: China's buying did not follow stronger ironmaking. Pig iron and coke output fell 3.1% and 1.3% year on year in January-October; October declines were 4.1% and 6.2%.

children.title: Steel exports show which markets the output depends on
section_path: Steel exports show which markets the output depends on
children.section_path_text: Steel exports show which markets the output depends on
children.summary: China made 2.8% less steel in January-October but shipped 6.8% more by sea, 89.0 Mt against 83.2 Mt, and the increase widened to 28.4% between 1 September and 24 November. More of China's output therefore depends on export buyers and on trade policy.

children.title: Follow the mill and the loading programme
section_path: Follow the mill and the loading programme
children.section_path_text: Follow the mill and the loading programme
children.summary: Australian shipments assigned to JFE's Fukuyama works were level with last year at 4.5 Mt in the year to 24 November. Nippon Steel's Kashima works took 1.9 Mt against 2.2 Mt and Hyundai Steel's Dangjin works 2.5 Mt against 3.4 Mt.

children.title: Gladstone congestion remains elevated
children.summary: Gladstone averaged 45.5 dry bulk vessels waiting to load over 1-24 November, against 27.9 a year earlier and 32.7 in September (Figure 4). Coal vessels that finished waiting in November had waited 18.8 days on average, against 12.5 days a year earlier.

children.title: Freight: Capesize is firm, Pacific Panamax is softer
section_path: Freight: Capesize is firm, Pacific Panamax is softer
children.section_path_text: Freight: Capesize is firm, Pacific Panamax is softer
children.summary: The Baltic Exchange Capesize time-charter average was USD 41,314 a day on 24 November, up 11.1% on the week and 37.4% in four weeks. The Panamax Pacific round voyage was 7.4% lower over four weeks at USD 19,166 a day.

children.title: Panamax and Post-Panamax lead the increase
section_path: Panamax and Post-Panamax lead the increase
children.section_path_text: Panamax and Post-Panamax lead the increase
children.summary: Panamax and Post-Panamax vessels carried 16.2 Mt of Australian Coking Coal to China over 1 January-24 November 2026, against 6.9 Mt over the same 2025 dates (Figure 5). Repeat Chinese orders therefore matter for these vessel classes.

children.title: The four-week outlook
children.summary: Through 22 December, the base case is an uneven loading recovery. Falling Gladstone queues alongside stronger departures would improve execution.
